groups.title: Capsule (E03500ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults (aged 15 years and over): take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occur; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, swelling, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like) or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics or thiazide diuretics. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or — rarely — signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome — severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), asthma, impaired liver function (general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) and the like), interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like), reduced urine output with swelling of the face and limbs, heavy eyelids, stiff hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, or myopathy (weakness, cramp of the arms or legs, paralysis) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (300300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B1 and vitamin B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness, and to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi and eye fatigue.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 8 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day, or 2 tablets at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are under a doctor's care.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine together with levodopa.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools or diarrhoea appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E07200ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, and in old age; to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal symptoms such as stiff shoulders and neck, numb hands and feet and cold hands and feet, and neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; for beriberi and eye fatigue; to relieve pigmentation caused by sunlight, skin disease and the like; and to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; or if you have gout or kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, nausea, vomiting or loose stools appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral liquid (124531ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for primary and secondary carnitine deficiency and for disturbance of heart muscle metabolism caused by ischaemic heart disease such as angina and acute myocardial infarction.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 to 3 g a day, divided into 2 to 3 doses. The dose may be increased or decreased as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding.

Dilute the medicine before taking it by mouth.

Temporary nausea or vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, body odour, rash, hives or facial swelling may occur.

groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soy or peanuts; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function or low blood protein; if you have gout, or have or have had kidney stones; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), loose stools, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid on the lungs appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D62700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to prevent and relieve the dizziness, vomiting and headache caused by motion sickness.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Children aged 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet at a time. The number of doses is limited to 2 in 1 day. To prevent motion sickness, take a dose 30 minutes to 1 hour before boarding. If a further dose is needed, take one dose leaving an interval of at least 4 hours. Let the tablet dissolve in the mouth or chew it.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their phenylalanine intake.

Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding, if the user is a child aged 7 years or under, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms from a medicine (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have a heart disorder, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are frail; if the user is an older person; if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other anti-emetics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, antitussives and expectorants, or gastrointestinal analgesics and antispasmodics. Avoid alcoholic drinks while taking this medicine.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, headache, facial flushing, sensitivity to light, difficulty passing urine, thirst or constipation appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E95500ACS)

groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day it may cause birth defects. Women who are less than 3 months pregnant or who may be pregnant must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil or have had an allergic reaction to it; or if you have hypersensitivity to soy or peanuts.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied in sufficient amounts by a normal diet, so do not let the supplementary dose exceed 5,000 IU a day. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with anti-aldosterone medicines, triamterene or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful swollen joints, loose stools, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, fluid on the lungs, constipation, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, red spots, hives, eczema, rash, a maculopapular rash, itching, swelling, or swelling and fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
